title: Region and division-pair controls retained distinct structure links for task coding and spiking in 171 mouse brain regions
abstract: We tested whether regional resemblance explains a reported split between wiring, cell-type mix and physiology. We rebuilt predictors for the same 171 IBL mouse brain regions and 14,535 region pairs. We added fixed effects for each region and each unordered brain-division pair. With region effects, input similarity had a task-coding coefficient of 0.185, while cell-mix similarity had a spiking coefficient of 0.326. With both control sets, the values were 0.210 and 0.194. Coding cell-mix estimates stayed near zero. Region effects reduced unique input variance for spiking by 75%, while the coding value stayed near 0.64%. These controls retained the distinct links in the measured data. This is a reanalysis, not independent replication or a causal result. Region jackknife intervals condition on fixed sources. Secondary surrogate tests had imperfect long-distance variogram matching and do not establish calibrated wiring specificity. The package provides code, model statistics, null draws, source hashes and retrieval instructions. External source records and derived Allen databases are kept outside the bundle.
